decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with through contacts build on core polishing and drilling know-how. They fit the announced push into multifunctional packaging wafers, so sunk R&D and strategic centrality argue for persisting.

Carrier wafers for thin and small-diameter wafer handling sit at the heart of the firm's stated direction toward reusable carriers. This makes the product a core commitment rather than an expendable experiment.

The copper interposer glass wafer was given its own web page, a visible public commitment. It aligns with advanced packaging trends, so any weak early demand can be blamed on the temporary market and pandemic disruptions of 2020 and 2021.
The off-the-shelf brand is close to the established business and cheap to maintain. Having been launched publicly as a branded line, management would keep it to justify the branding investment.

Glass-based circuit boards are distant from the core offer and hence the most at risk. Still, the R&D invested and the possible link to EU-funded projects let management attribute weak results to slow market adoption and persist for now.
